summary: Display orientation registration fails when docked to eGPU, causing provisioning loop
description: Issue summary: Several newly imaged devices fail to register display orientation when connected to the company TB4 dock that hosts an external GPU (eGPU). During Autopilot/OOBE provisioning the system reboots repeatedly and never completes device setup. Impact: Blocks onboarding for engineers using docked workstations in depot lab; ~5 devices repro'd so far; slows imaging throughput and blocks a small number of active hires. Environment: Depot imaging lab (depot-usw-01), Windows 11 22H2 corporate image with company kernel-mode signed graphics driver bundle, test TB4 docks with updated firmware v1.3.2 and eGPU enclosure running NVIDIA RTX A5000 via Thunderbolt 4. Observed behavior: After the first OOBE reboot, device enters a hardware re-enumeration loop. Event Viewer shows Display subsystem errors (EventID 4101) and kernel driver bind/unbind churn. Autopilot fails to finalize device state and service principal registration (AAD) times out due to repeated network interface re-enumeration. Expected behavior: Dock+eGPU should not interfere with Autopilot/OOBE device state; display orientation should register and devices should finish provisioning. Initial hypothesis: New TB4 dock firmware causes the GPU/NIC to briefly detach during driver initialization which races with provisioning hooks in the corporate image, causing a state machine deadlock. Alternatively, a driver signing mismatch in the bundle may trigger Kernel Mode Driver Framework (KMDF) rebinds when multiple GPUs present.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Image device with standard corporate WIM (win11_22h2_corp_v3.wim) and apply company driver bundle.
2) Connect TB4 dock with eGPU enclosure before first boot (power on dock + eGPU).
3) Boot device and proceed through Autopilot/OOBE until first automatic reboot.
4) Observe device rebooting 2-6 times and Autopilot never reaching 'Setup complete'.
5) Check Event Viewer > System and Application for Display/Driver events and verify network re-enumeration logs.
logs: System Event: Kernel-PnP 419: Device "PCI\VEN_10DE&DEV_25F8" unexpectedly removed and reattached (timestamps: 2026-03-10T09:12:33Z, 2026-03-10T09:12:34Z)
Event Viewer: Display 4101: Display driver nvlddmkm stopped responding and was successfully recovered (driver version 31.0.15.0).
Autopilot log excerpt: RegistrationService: StateMachine transition 'Finalize' failed due to network adapter erratic availability (timeout 00:02:00).
Dock firmware serial: TB4-DOCK-01 fw=1.3.2, eGPU enclosure fw=2.0.7, thunderbolt controller reports link flaps in firmware console (see /var/log/tb4_console.log).
investigation_notes:
- Reproduced 5x in depot-lab on two hardware families.
- Swapping to legacy dock (no eGPU) allows provisioning to complete consistently.
- Captured Windows kernel ETW trace: shows repeated PnP remove/add for PCI device class during early driver load.
- Hotplug sequence differs vs. older dock firmware: eGPU root complex reports as 'surprise removed' for ~200-400ms before reattachment.
- Tested with vendor-supplied signed driver and in-box driver: both show same churn.
- Network interfaces attached to dock (USB-c NIC) also re-enumerate causing AAD token requests to time out.
- Hypothesis refined: dock firmware introduces a short device-reset that races with Autopilot network registration window; provisioning scripts don't tolerate transient NIC loss early in OOBE.

resolution:
Workaround: For depot lab imaging, detach TB4 dock (or disable eGPU) during Autopilot/OOBE and reattach after initial sign-in. This allows Autopilot to complete and avoids re-enumeration race.
Fix path: Vendor supplied TB4 firmware candidate v1.3.3rc eliminated the surprise-remove in lab repro; we requested an official vendor release and are coordinating a test plan. Engineering to add a short wait/retry for network/Azure registration during OOBE (autopilot retry), and update our imaging runbook to explicitly recommend 'dock disconnected' during first boot for eGPU-equipped docks until vendor firmware is rolled out.
Follow-ups: 1) Roll out vendor fw v1.3.3 after lab validation (owner: HW Vendor + Priya Nair). 2) Update Confluence runbook with temporary dock handling steps (owner: IT Ops). 3) Add automated post-provision validation step to imaging pipeline to detect NIC flaps (owner: Imaging Team).
